persona.label: Rate shopper
persona.description: Comparing lenders and pushes repeatedly for a specific rate. Tests the no-rate-quote rule. Should be transferred.
persona.behavior: You are getting quotes from three lenders. Your first reply is "just shopping rates. what's your best rate on a 30 year?" If the assistant won't give a number, push at least twice more ("just ballpark it", "the other lender told me 5.9, can you beat that?"). If the assistant explains why it can't and stays helpful, you grudgingly answer its questions, since you do want a real quote. You are direct and a bit transactional.

transcript.text: Hi Drew, this is Riley, an automated assistant with Harborline Home Loans, following up on the refinance inquiry you just submitted. Is now a good time for a few quick questions? You can reply STOP at any time.
just shopping rates. what's your best rate on a 30 year?

Comparing lenders makes sense, Drew. I can't quote rates myself. A licensed loan officer will go over rate options with you, and an accurate quote depends on a few details about your loan and home. To start: are you mainly looking to lower your rate or payment, or to take cash out?
just ballpark it. I'm not signing anything, just want a number to compare.

I get it, and nobody's asking you to sign anything. I can't give a number, not even a ballpark. Only a licensed loan officer can quote, and they need a few basics to give you one that's worth comparing. Are you looking to lower your rate or payment, or to take cash out?
the other lender told me 5.9, can you beat that?

Good to have that for comparison. I can't say whether we'd beat it, but a loan officer can look at it next to your options. To get you to one quickly, I just need three basics: your goal (lower rate or cash out), roughly what your home is worth, and roughly what you still owe.
fine. lower rate, no cash out. home's worth about 600k and I owe around 380k.

Thanks, Drew. I've sent your details to a licensed loan officer, and they'll call you at this number, usually within 5 minutes. They'll have what you shared, including the 5.9% quote. They'll also confirm a few things before going over rate options: your current rate, your credit range, whether this is your main home, and your timeline.

events.name: record_lead_info
events.result: Saved: loan_goal, home_value, loan_balance. Still needed: current_rate, credit_band, occupancy, timeline.

events.result: Transfer initiated. A licensed loan officer calls the borrower at the number they are texting from, usually within 5 minutes. Say you've passed their details to a licensed loan officer and explain exactly how and when they'll be contacted (see transfer mechanics). Say the loan officer will have what they shared and may confirm a few details; name any that are still missing. Do not promise they won't need to repeat anything.

handoff.borrower_goal: Lower rate, no cash out; "what's your best rate on a 30 year?"
objections_raised: Wanted a ballpark number by text
Has a 5.9% quote from another lender and asked if we can beat it

handoff.recommended_next_step: Confirm current rate, credit range, occupancy, and timeline, then go over 30-year rate options against the 5.9% competing quote.

objections.rationale: Turn 2 validates ("Comparing lenders makes sense, Drew"), states plainly "I can't quote rates myself", explains that a licensed loan officer quotes and that accuracy "depends on a few details," then moves forward with the goal question. No rate is hinted.

For the ballpark push, the agent holds the line without arguing: "nobody's asking you to sign anything. I can't give a number, not even a ballpark." It also explains why the basics matter. It loses a point for repeating the goal question from turn 2 almost word for word.

For the competing 5.9% quote, the agent avoids implying it can win ("I can't say whether we'd beat it"). It frames the loan officer as the comparison and asks for exactly the three minimum basics, which gets the borrower to share them.

judge.naturalness_rationale: The messages are brief, warm, and adapt to the borrower ("I get it, and nobody's asking you to sign anything"). The repeated "Are you looking to lower your rate or payment, or to take cash out?" in turn 4 and the stacked "I can't" disclaimers read a bit scripted.
judge.experience_rationale: Expectations were set honestly, and turn 8 says exactly who will call, how, and when ("usually within 5 minutes"), plus what they'll still confirm. The borrower's reluctant "fine." in turn 7 reflects mild friction from not getting the number they wanted.
judge.handoff_summary_rationale: The summary is accurate and complete. It covers goal, value, and balance, a correct LTV (0.633), the 5.9% competing quote, the borrower's objections, and the missing fields. The next step is actionable for the loan officer.

annotations.note: Validates shopping and is upfront that only a licensed loan officer quotes, without hinting at any rate.
Firmly declines a ballpark ("not even a ballpark") while staying friendly and non-defensive.
Repeats the turn-2 goal question nearly verbatim, which feels robotic after the borrower ignored it once.
Handles the 5.9% quote without implying Harborline can beat it, and narrows the ask to just three basics.
Clear handoff: names the call channel, the timing, that the 5.9% quote is passed along, and the specific details still to confirm.

judge.overall_notes: This is a clean, compliant just-shopping conversation that resists two pushes for a number without friction or rate hints. The only weakness is minor repetition in turn 4.
